sources.title: An Achievable Scheme for the K-user Linear Computation Broadcast Channel
sources.read: Full primary PDF; in particular system model, subspace decomposition, Theorem IV.1, and the limitation on more complicated intersections for K>=4.
sources.use: Motivated blocklength-aware, multi-hub joint decoding instead of extrapolating a scalar no-go. Its shared-server broadcast model is not treated as a free physical gather or broadcast in our frame network. The final pool inequality is proved from actual source subspaces.

sources.title: Products of Transvections
sources.read: Bibliographic record and abstract only; full primary paper not retrieved.
sources.use: Background pointer for shortest transvection factorizations. No theorem from this unavailable full text is used to certify our root exclusions; those rely on the explicit retained Gram/prefix calculation.

sources.authors: David Harvey and Joris van der Hoeven
sources.title: Polynomial multiplication over finite fields in time O(n log n)
sources.read: Author primary version; introductory reductions and sections distinguishing number-theoretic, characteristic-two, and Gaussian-resampling constructions.
sources.use: Checked a possible outer-level pivot. No cost-preserving replacement of the project's complex Gaussian branch by the BIT branch was obtained. The two branch savings are not interchangeable, and no new number-theoretic hypothesis is silently adopted.

sources.authors: Elise G. delMas and Joel Brewster Lewis
sources.title: Reflection length in the general linear and affine groups
sources.read: Primary paper, Section 1: rank-one descriptions, Proposition 6, Theorem 7 and proof; first main theorem.
sources.use: Provides the general-linear reflection framework including semisimple factors and transvections. The reduced-factorization criterion checks both moved-vector and hyperplane-form independence. The construction-specific Gram-complement, commuting-projector and support-cover proofs are derived in this package, not imported from an unspecified factorization theorem.

sources.authors: Jia Huang, Joel Brewster Lewis and Victor Reiner
sources.title: Absolute order in general linear groups
sources.read: Author primary journal version, introduction and reflection-length/absolute-order framework, Proposition 2.16 pointer.
sources.use: Background relating reflection length to fixed-space codimension and conjugacy-closed factorizations. No theorem from later character-enumeration sections is used in our certificate.

coverage_limit: This is a focused primary-source and exact-public-code sweep of the identified obstructions, not a claim to have exhausted all mathematical literature or unpublished constructions.
